notes:
I don't have any notes on Jeremiah 8 to give you, because the research didn't go through.

I sent requests for six pages: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, and the NET Bible notes. My script had a bug and crashed before it could show me any of the text. When I tried to fix it, I was told I had no tool calls left for this turn. I never read any source.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So any notes I wrote now would break those rules, and I've written none.

**If you ask again, here is what I'll do:**
1. **Main reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub or StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** check each tradition's own sites, such as Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Spurgeon on spurgeon.org, and Ligonier or The Gospel Coalition for the Reformed view. The likeliest verses are v. 11 ("Peace, peace" and false comfort), v. 20 ("The harvest has passed… we have not been saved," a favourite revival-preaching text) and v. 22 ("balm in Gilead").
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for modern scholarship (for example on "the lying pen of the scribes" in v. 8, and on who is speaking in vv. 18–22), and New Advent or other Catholic and Orthodox sources if they cover the chapter. For popular modern teaching, I'll only include something if a source on your list actually discusses it.

Each point will have its URL, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
